newsitem.title: INDIA: India PM says no leadership change in ruling front.
newsitem.headline: India PM says no leadership change in ruling front.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, facing a crisis after the Congress party withdrew critical support to his coalition, was quoted on Wednesday as saying his alliance would not agree to a change in leadership.
But he expressed hope that "some positive" solution would emerge from discussions between his United Front alliance and the Congress after the two parties agreed to hold talks.
"The United Front has already decided that there will be no change in leadership. This issue is not negotiable," Deve Gowda was quoted by the Press Trust of India (PTI) as telling reporters.
The ruling United Front invited Congress for formal talks on Wednesday ahead of a vote of confidence that the minority government is scheduled to face in parliament on Friday.
The Congress party has said it is willing to support the United Front government if Deve Gowda is replaced as the parliamentary leader of the centre-left alliance.
The Congress offered support to the coalition last year to defeat a 12-day-old government formed by the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The Congress accused Deve Gowda of not containing "communal forces," a reference to the BJP, the Congress party's arch-rival.
PTI said Gowda described as "a positive step" a decision by the two groups to start talks to resolve differences.
